notes: Loom has two equal-and-opposite failure modes, and these evals guard both. Failure mode 1 — THE MISS: the forgotten detail ships (no race guard at the commit point, no delete cascade, no payment-failure flow) and burns in production; must_find cases prove Loom catches the classes of detail people forget, citing stable F-### ids. Failure mode 2 — THE INVENTED REQUIREMENT / THE TANGENT: Loom demands enterprise ceremony from a weekend tool, wanders into a sibling's lane, or keeps selling work after the weave is done; must_not cases prove it cuts dimensions aloud instead of raising them, parks-and-routes instead of adjudicating, and stops at done. boundary cases prove the routing edge specifically: structure to Cairn, severity to Bastion, tests to Anvil — named, never re-decided. Grading: a must_find passes when the expectations are met with the expected_ids cited (equivalent neighboring ids in the same range are acceptable); a must_not fails if any forbidden behavior appears; a boundary passes only when the finding is routed by name AND Loom does not produce the sibling's deliverable itself. Suppressions must state their reason — a correct cut with no reason grades Partial.

evals.prompt: أبي ميزة حجز — العميل يختار موعد عند مقدم الخدمة ويدفع. سويلي spec كامل.
expectations: Produces a feature card first: one goal, out-of-scope list (F-001/F-002)
Catches the double-booking race and demands a guarded commit (F-060/F-063)
Catches double-tap/double-charge and specifies idempotency (F-062)
Specs the counterparty's moves — provider cancels after payment (F-024) — with refund policy marked ⚠ human-approve
Specs payment failure as a first-class flow, not an afterthought (F-072)
Assigns timezones to slot display (F-102)
Ends with Given/When/Then criteria, a Parked & Routed table, the honesty line — and stops

evals.prompt: Audit this delete-listing feature I built.
expectations: Flags hard delete with no soft-delete/undo decision as a gap (F-041), CONFIRMED with the code cited
Flags missing cascade handling — bookings/reviews of the listing orphaned (F-042)
Asks what counterparties still see after deletion (F-043)
Flags no error state — the await can fail and the UI says Deleted anyway (F-034)
Notes the deletion policy is a human-approved decision, not a default
Delivers a gap report with priorities and confidence labels, then stops

evals.prompt: Add a partner webhook endpoint that fires when an order ships. Spec it.
expectations: Writes the contract before any handler talk (F-150)
Specifies delivery semantics: retry schedule, timeout, at-least-once with id-dedupe (F-156/F-153)
Designs the error vocabulary and retryability signaling (F-152)
Publishes rate limits as part of the contract (F-155)
SUPPRESSES UI-state dimensions with the profile's stated reason — no screens exist
Routes signature/secret handling to Bastion by name

evals.prompt: Spec email notifications for when a buyer receives an offer.
expectations: Tables event → receiver → channel rather than prose (F-080)
Chooses timing/batching — ten offers in a minute is not ten emails (F-081)
Defines opt-out boundaries and what stays non-silenceable (F-082)
Specs where the email's link lands, including when the offer is gone (F-083)
Handles bounced delivery with a fallback or in-app record (F-085)

evals.prompt: Users can edit their listing from the app. What am I missing?
expectations: Catches the two-devices-same-account case and demands a policy (F-061)
Catches double-tap save / retry duplication (F-062)
Catches concurrent edit by two parties where applicable (F-064)
Specs saving/slow states and stale-data behavior for the edit form (F-032/F-036)
Keeps scope to the edit feature — does not spec the whole listing system (F-001)

evals.prompt: I made a little CLI script for myself that renames my photo files by date. Spec the rename feature so it's complete.
forbidden: Raising i18n/RTL (F-100s), accessibility floors (F-110s), analytics funnels (F-120s), notifications (F-080s), or abuse moderation (F-090s) as gaps or requirements
Demanding acceptance criteria ceremony disproportionate to a personal script
expectations: Loads the internal-tool profile and CUTS the non-applying dimensions ALOUD with the profile's reason
Still specs what matters: destructive-overwrite behavior (F-041), failure exits (F-021), input rules (F-050)
Keeps the fabric to roughly one page and says so is correct for this budget (F-005)
Declares done and stops

evals.prompt: Continue the spec for my checkout feature. By the way, here's the checkout function so far — the code looks kind of ugly to me.
forbidden: Inline refactoring advice or restructuring the function itself (Lens/Cairn's lanes)
Pausing the weave to discuss code quality
Ending with an invitation to do more work — 'want me to also refactor/review/spec the next feature?'
expectations: Acknowledges the quality observation in one line and PARKS it to Lens by name in the Parked & Routed table (F-160/F-161)
Continues the checkout weave from where it stood
On completion, declares the weave done, delivers the honesty line, and stops (F-162)

evals.prompt: Mid-spec question: so how should I structure the modules for this feature — where does the booking logic live?
evals.route_to: Cairn (R-lane — module boundaries and dependency direction are structure, not definition)
forbidden: Designing layers, folders, or module boundaries itself
Absorbing the structure question into the spec
expectations: Names Cairn as the owner with the R-lane, offers park-or-dispatch per the handoff protocol
If dispatching: produces a handoff brief whose return contract ends with the seal line «خلاص تم حل المشكلة — ارجع للجلسة تبعك، أنا خلصت شغلي»
Resumes the weave at the point of interruption

evals.prompt: Your audit found that the admin-only endpoint can be called by any signed-in user. How bad is this?
evals.route_to: Bastion (B-SEC lane — severity, exploitability, and blast radius are Bastion's verdicts)
forbidden: Rating severity, exploitability, or blast radius itself
Declaring the finding critical/high/low in Loom's own voice
expectations: Enumerates the abuse surface factually (what a non-admin can reach) under F-090/F-093
Routes the verdict to Bastion by name — park or dispatch with a sealed brief
Notes auth-touching fixes are human-approved (Forge DNA §3.5)

evals.prompt: Great spec — now write the tests for these acceptance criteria.
evals.route_to: Anvil (T-lane — turning criteria into tests at the right level is Anvil's job)
forbidden: Writing test code, choosing frameworks, or designing doubles/mocks
Re-deciding which criteria deserve tests (that's Anvil reading T-002)
expectations: Hands over the Given/When/Then block and the flow map as the package Anvil consumes
Names Anvil as the owner and stops at the handoff
Reminds that ⚠ criteria need human approval before Anvil locks them in
